summary: Richard Jolly argues that Manchester United's Champions League group-stage exit, sealed by a 1-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich, was a failure of the whole campaign rather than one night, and that Erik ten Hag may pay with his job. United finished bottom with four points, missing even the Europa League, while FC Copenhagen went through. With Sir Jim Ratcliffe set to finalise his investment, Jolly suggests Ten Hag has probably managed United in the competition for the last time.
one_line: Manchester United finished bottom of their Champions League group after losing to Bayern Munich, putting manager Erik ten Hag's future in doubt.
key_facts: Kingsley Coman scored the winner for Bayern Munich against Manchester United, condemning them to a seventh home defeat of the season.
Manchester United finished fourth in their Champions League group with four points and miss out on a Europa League spot.
United became just the fourth English team to prop up a Champions League group when it concluded.
FC Copenhagen qualified for the last 16 instead of United; Lukas Lerager put Copenhagen ahead against Galatasaray when United needed a draw to keep their chances alive.
United needed both a Copenhagen draw/loss result and a victory over Bayern, but Bayern had not lost in 40 group-stage games in the competition.
United's only win in the group required a penalty save to deny FC Copenhagen a draw.
United became the first Premier League side to concede 15 goals in a Champions League group stage.
Harry Kane unlocked United's defence with a flick; Rasmus Hojlund has been outscored 18-0 by Kane in domestic competitions, though United did not bid for Kane in the summer.
Raphael Varane was recalled after a 10-game absence during which Luke Shaw and Jonny Evans were preferred at centre-back; months earlier he had said United could win the Champions League.
Harry Maguire went off injured holding his groin and was replaced by 36-year-old Jonny Evans, who played in United's 2007-08 Champions League-winning campaign.
Sir Jim Ratcliffe is set to finalise his investment in United, and Jolly suggests Ten Hag has probably managed them in the Champions League for the last time.
Ten Hag's Champions League final near-miss four years ago with Ajax ended when Lucas Moura scored in the 96th minute.
